divergences.old: jira schema --example-only printing the bare example with no envelope
divergences.toil: The flag stays; the example comes back as data in the usual envelope, so with the flag data is the example itself, not { schema, example }. Save .data to use it as an --input-file
divergences.why: Every command writes exactly one envelope, so an agent never has to guess which shape stdout holds. The allowed fields are excused only for calls with --example-only (`when`), so plain jira schema must still return both.

divergences.old: jira download-attachment fetching the attachment's content URL, with the token, from whatever host Jira names
divergences.toil: The token goes only to baseUrl's origin: a content URL on another host has its path and query re-pointed at baseUrl, with a JIRA_ATTACHMENT_HOST warning
divergences.why: A server-supplied URL must not carry the user's credential to a host they didn't configure. A change a principle requires, so the integration makes it before a live run (CLAUDE.md, The command contract).

divergences.old: jira download-attachment reporting saved with the platform's separator
divergences.toil: saved uses forward slashes on every platform; the file lands in the same place
divergences.why: Paths in JSON output are identical on Windows, macOS and Linux (CLAUDE.md, Cross-Platform). Same on macOS and Linux as before.

divergences.old: jira download-attachment writing to a file that already exists
divergences.toil: Refused with INVALID_INPUT naming the path; the existing file is left alone. The contract replaced it (#70 item 8)
divergences.why: A read-only command, whose file name comes from whoever uploaded the attachment, must not change files already on disk.
